In one sentence: an enlisted post that operates and maintains an aircraft carrier's launch, arrest and recovery equipment and the deck work around it, and that must both hold the equipment state and deck safety and turn the operating orders, signal direction and records into actions that can be executed and checked.

The tasks of aircraft launch and recovery specialists fall into three categories: equipment operation and maintenance (operating and maintaining hydraulic and steam catapults, arresting gear, barriers, jet blast deflectors and cooling panels, installing and maintaining visual landing-aid equipment, and using electrical and mechanical test equipment and hand tools to test and maintain launch and recovery equipment), deck operation execution (directing aircraft launch and recovery by hand signal or light signal, starting the airfield arresting system such as the barrier and the arresting cable on an emergency landing, and completing the deck work to the post's division of duties), and records and state management (recording the launch, recovery and equipment maintenance logs, checking the equipment state against the checklist and reporting deviations). Unlike a planning and directing post, this occupation is mainly hands-on operation, testing and maintenance, and requires keeping the actions accurate and following the safety procedure.

subject.summary: Aircraft launch and recovery specialists are enlisted posts that operate and maintain an aircraft carrier's catapults, arresting gear and related mechanical, hydraulic and control systems, carry out deck operations and keep the records, and are responsible for installing and maintaining visual landing-aid equipment, for equipment testing and maintenance, for starting an emergency arrest and for directing by signal; the judgement focuses on enlistment conditions, equipment operating authorisation, safety procedure and the responsibility to stop the operation.
